findings.title: Rendering a DOCX with a renamed numbering part can exhaust the process stack
findings.summary: A document author can point the internal numbering relationship at deeply nested XML named `numbering.bin`. Admission skips XML depth and tag policy for that auxiliary filename, but the renderer parses it recursively, allowing a compact DOCX to terminate the conversion process.

severity.rationale: Attacker-controlled document data deterministically bypasses the depth policy and can abort a local conversion or an embedding worker. Exposure is constrained to a caller choosing to process that document; no remote service or cross-tenant deployment is established, and SECURITY.md recommends process CPU/memory limits.
severity.changeConditions: A shared service accepting public document uploads without per-job process isolation would increase operational impact; enforcing XML limits at each semantic consumer removes this path.

confidence.rationale: Static trace connects the extension-based admission decision, relationship-selected numbering part and unchecked recursive parser. No runtime trigger was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Render entry admits package
codeEvidence.explanation: Caller-controlled DOCX bytes are admitted before the same bytes are normalized and opened.

codeEvidence.label: Admission chooses XML by extension
codeEvidence.explanation: Only .xml and .rels entries receive XML policy checks; a numbering.bin entry is treated as binary.

codeEvidence.label: Only the main part has an extension exception
codeEvidence.explanation: The extra check for non-XML names applies to the main document, leaving auxiliary relationship targets unchecked.

codeEvidence.label: Numbering relationship controls the selected part
codeEvidence.explanation: The document's internal numbering relationship selects an arbitrary package part, excluding external targets but imposing no XML policy.

codeEvidence.label: Selected numbering bytes reach permissive parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: The selected part is decoded as text and passed to the recursive DOM parser without checked parsing.

codeEvidence.label: DOM recursion has no depth argument
codeEvidence.explanation: Each nested element recursively invokes parse_element; the skipped admission depth bound is the only protection on this path.

rootCause.summary: `admit()` classifies XML by filename and only adds a nonstandard-extension exception for the main part. `main_rel_part()` trusts internal relationship targets, so `load_numbering()` can select an auxiliary `.bin` part. `parse_numbering_xml()` invokes the permissive DOM parser, whose element recursion has no depth limit, without validating the selected bytes.

findings.remediation: Apply the active XML depth/tag limits to every relationship-selected part immediately before DOM parsing, regardless of filename, and use bounded or iterative parsing as defense in depth.

limitations: No malicious file was generated or executed.
Other XML consumers were not exhaustively enumerated; this finding establishes the numbering path.
validation.summary: Verified that `with_layout()` admits input, `admit()` omits XML checks on non-.xml/.rels auxiliary entries, `main_rel_part()` selects the attacker-controlled internal target, and `load_numbering()` parses it without a second check. PartFs inflation caps and strict translation constrain bytes but do not validate the auxiliary XML nesting.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> admission extension filter -> internal numbering relationship -> part_string -> parse_numbering_xml -> recursive parse_element
dataflow.source: attacker-controlled package relationship and auxiliary part bytes

impact.why: A stack overflow aborts the processing worker.

likelihood.why: Requires the victim to process attacker-provided DOCX; no public deployment is assumed.

limitations: Process isolation contains the failure to the selected job.

reachability.summary: Any caller processing a document supplied by a lower-trust author through the public render API can reach this path; neither external relationship fetching nor filesystem access is required.
reachability.entrypoint: convert::docx_to_pdf and the shared layout pipeline

attackPath.summary: Supply a valid DOCX whose numbering relationship targets a `.bin` entry containing deeply nested elements, then call `docx_to_pdf()` or another renderer using the shared layout pipeline.

remediationTests: Render a DOCX with a deeply nested `numbering.bin` relationship target and assert an INVALID_XML refusal before DOM construction.
Retain support for nonstandard auxiliary filenames within the configured XML limits.

originalCandidate.title: Non-XML numbering relationship target bypasses admission depth checking
originalCandidate.originalEvidence: src/admission.rs:534 selects XML by suffix and :543 checks depth only in that branch; :555-569 exception applies only main part. src/convert/mod.rs:6557-6570 load_numbering resolves relationship target via main_rel_part (:21310-21319) and parses it with dom.parse_xdocument. src/xmllinq/parse.rs:660-661 recursively parses without local depth check. Baseline proposed internal numbering.bin with deeply nested elements.

originalFinding.title: Related XML parts with non-XML extensions bypass depth admission and reach recursive parsing
originalFinding.attacker: An attacker supplying a DOCX for PDF/PNG rendering.
originalFinding.violated_security_invariant: Every untrusted XML part must satisfy the configured XML depth limit before recursive DOM construction.
originalFinding.source_to_sink: Admission checks XML depth only for names ending in .xml or .rels, with an additional exception solely for the main document. The renderer resolves the numbering relationship to an arbitrary internal target, loads that target as XML regardless of extension, and passes it directly to the recursive permissive parser.
originalFinding.impact: A small DOCX containing a numbering relationship targeting numbering.bin with sufficiently deep nested elements can exhaust the native process stack or trap its WASM instance. Native Python consumers can lose their entire hosting process.
supporting_source_evidence: Admission sets is_xml = lower.ends_with(".xml") || lower.ends_with(".rels"); other entries are drained without check_xml_depth.
main_rel_part resolves an internal relationship target without requiring an XML filename.
load_numbering calls parse_numbering_xml on the resolved part; parse_numbering_xml calls dom.parse_xdocument(xml).
Parser::parse_element recursively invokes self.parse_element(scope) for child elements without a local depth check.
counterevidence: ZIP compressed/inflated byte limits remain effective, but deeply nested XML requires little input space.
Admission separately checks a main part with an unusual extension; that exception does not cover numbering or other auxiliary parts.
Checked inspect parsing validates related XML separately, but rendering uses the unchecked parser.
No application code was executed; the conclusion follows the static call chain.
originalFinding.remediation: Apply XML policy to every part consumed as XML regardless of its filename, preferably at a common checked part-loading boundary. Enforce depth during DOM construction as defense in depth.

findings.title: Importing a cyclic drawing payload can terminate Markdown conversion
findings.summary: A Markdown author can supply a `drawing:` image payload with a dependency that points to itself. JSON decoding accepts that graph and package assembly recursively materializes it without tracking visited dependencies, exhausting the conversion process stack.

severity.rationale: A small attacker-supplied Markdown image payload can abort a caller processing it, including native or WASM conversion. This is a constrained document-processing availability failure; remote multi-user deployment is not established and process quotas are a caller obligation.
severity.changeConditions: A shared unisolated Markdown conversion service would increase impact; rejecting cycles or memoizing in-progress parts removes the deterministic trigger.

confidence.rationale: Independent source trace verifies direct public Markdown acceptance, unvalidated dependency indices, and recursive traversal with no cycle guard; no application code was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Public Markdown conversion
codeEvidence.explanation: The public API accepts the caller's Markdown, including drawing destinations.

codeEvidence.label: Drawing destination decoded without graph validation
codeEvidence.explanation: Base64 JSON becomes Drawing with caller-selected dependency indices; deserialization supplies no graph traversal control.

codeEvidence.label: Decoded drawing enters the output model
codeEvidence.explanation: The writer accepts a drawing URL and stores the decoded structure for package assembly.

codeEvidence.label: Package assembly walks root dependencies
codeEvidence.explanation: An internal relationship with a valid dependency index invokes dep_part.

codeEvidence.label: Dependency traversal recurses before recording a completed part
codeEvidence.explanation: The function records only chosen output names and recursively follows valid inner indices without visited or in-progress graph state.

codeEvidence.label: Package emitter calls materialize
codeEvidence.explanation: Package emission passes the attacker-supplied Drawing to the recursive materializer.

rootCause.summary: `picture()` accepts a decoded `Drawing` from caller-controlled Markdown and package assembly invokes `materialize()`. Root relationships select dependency indices. `dep_part()` inserts a generated filename into `used`, but does not mark the dependency index as in progress or completed before following its relationships. A self-edge therefore re-enters the same dependency indefinitely; filename collision handling does not stop the graph recursion.

findings.remediation: Validate and bound the drawing dependency graph before assembly; use a per-index in-progress/completed map to reject cycles or allocate each output part once before resolving links.

limitations: No crafted input was generated or executed.
A valid captured graph cycle may also reproduce this, but the proven path is author-supplied Markdown.
validation.summary: Verified a single dependency with `rels[].part` pointing to its own valid index passes the only index checks. `dep_part()` recursively invokes itself before writing/comparing the part bytes. Capture-time MAX_DEPS and JSON nesting limits do not constrain this flat cyclic graph, and no graph validation is performed by decode().

dataflow.summary: caller Markdown -> picture -> drawing::decode -> document.drawings -> package::drawing -> materialize -> recursive dep_part
dataflow.outcome: stack exhaustion and process or WASM-instance termination

likelihood.why: Requires the victim to import the attacker's Markdown; no public service is assumed.

reachability.summary: Any consumer of the public Markdown-to-DOCX API that converts a document from a lower-trust author can trigger the path with default options; no local file or network access is required.

attackPath.summary: Pass Markdown containing a `drawing:` image URL whose decoded root relationship points to dependency 0 and whose dependency 0 relationship points back to 0 to `markdown_to_docx()`.

remediationTests: Import a self-referential dependency and a two-node cycle and assert bounded refusal or safe graph-preserving completion.
Import a shared acyclic dependency graph and assert each part is emitted once.

originalCandidate.evidence: Confirmed source mechanism in drawing payload restoration: untrusted Markdown drawing: JSON decodes without graph validation; materialize -> dep_part recursively follows rel.part indices with no visited/in-progress map. A dep referring to itself (or valid captured OPC dependency cycle) recurses indefinitely; MAX_DEPS only applies to capture, and used names never stop recursion. Gathering exact caller/line evidence.

originalFinding.title: Drawing payload dependency cycles cause unbounded recursive restoration
originalFinding.attacker: An attacker supplying Markdown to the public markdown_to_docx API, its bindings, or the Markdown conversion CLI.
originalFinding.violated_invariant: A small, structurally valid drawing payload must not select unbounded recursion in the host process.
dataflow: src/markdown/write.rs:59-62 exposes markdown_to_docx with attacker-controlled Markdown.
src/markdown/write.rs:4189-4197 accepts drawing: image destinations and stores their decoded Drawing.
src/markdown/from_docx/drawing.rs:1397-1408 performs base64 and serde JSON decoding without validating dependency graph structure.
src/markdown/package.rs:1702-1712 calls materialize, which follows the top-level rel.part index at drawing.rs:1889-1895.
dep_part at drawing.rs:1964-1974 recursively follows each dependency relationship's part index without tracking visited or in-progress indices.
originalFinding.impact: A payload containing one dependency whose relationship points back to itself repeatedly invokes dep_part until stack exhaustion or resource exhaustion terminates the conversion process, including an embedding host. Acyclic shared dependency graphs also receive repeated expansion because completed dependencies are not memoized.
source_evidence: drawing.rs:1408 returns serde_json::from_slice directly; the payload accepts arbitrary rels/deps indices.
drawing.rs:1965-1966 chooses a new name and inserts it into used, but used is a name-collision set and never rejects revisiting the same dependency index.
drawing.rs:1973-1974 accepts any inner index below drawing.deps.len() and recursively calls dep_part.
drawing.rs:1989-2004 checks existing bytes only after recursive dependency restoration, so the later deduplication cannot break cycles.
A minimal graph needs only a top-level relationship with part=0 and deps[0].rels[0].part=0; it does not require deeply nested JSON or XML.
counterevidence: Capture has MAX_DEPS=64, MAX_DEP_RELS=64, and MAX_DEP_BYTES=16 MiB, but these checks occur in Deps::dep_for at drawing.rs:591-620, not in decode or materialize.

A self-cycle fits all capture limits. Capture itself records the dependency index before recursively symbolizing it at drawing.rs:591-612, so captured package relationship cycles can also survive into a payload.
Malformed base64/JSON becomes alt text, but the cyclic graph is valid JSON.
No triggering input was executed; this conclusion is based on the complete recursive function and its callers.
originalFinding.remediation: Validate decoded payload budgets and indices. Restore dependencies through an index-to-output-name map with explicit in-progress/completed states. Either reject cycles with a typed error or allocate each dependency's destination once before wiring relationships. Memoize completed dependencies and bound total restored bytes.

surfaces.label: Release, CI and automated review privilege boundaries
surfaces.riskArea: CI trust and shared build cache
surfaces.notes: Focused reviewer found no ordinary contributor-to-release secret or direct shell-injection path. release.yml:15-21 is tag-only; release job owns contents:write at :230-265; artifact downloads are own-run at :230-250; signing temp keys cleaned at :261-309. scripts/release.sh:230-289 constrains version and :552-648 quotes summaries; eval at :1092-1100 receives fixed call strings. Jules workflows transfer metadata through env and reject fork heads before checkout (.github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:33-110,214-324; jules-review.yml:18-40). However PR CI executes repository/local-action code on self-hosted runners (.github/workflows/ci.yml:14-48,72-101,252-310; docs.yml:42-99; adoption.yml:16-31,48-102; md-roundtrip.yml:13-39). mbx action configures http://mbx-cache:7543 namespace jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines without a credential (.github/actions/mbx/action.yml:8-26,33-52), while comments claim protected-push-only publication. Actual server authorization, cache object integrity, network isolation, fork approval and ephemeral runner controls are absent and unresolved; client read mode does not prove server authorization. No confirmed poisoning/credential disclosure.

A ~1 MiB WordDocument text region referenced by 4096 consecutive 1 MiB CP pieces (same FC; ~48 KiB CLX; ccp_text near u32::MAX) drives read():195 to allocate billions of StoryChar records at main_text():1175-1220, before blocks. originalFinding.title: Legacy DOC piece-table reuse amplifies a small document into billions of decoded character records
originalFinding.attacker: An attacker supplying a legacy DOC to the library or native CLI.
originalFinding.violated_security_invariant: Decoded document content must remain within an explicit resource budget independent of physical input length.
originalFinding.source_to_sink: Each PCD independently chooses a physical WordDocument offset. main_text verifies increasing, contiguous CP coverage but permits many CP pieces to reuse the same physical character range. It then decodes every logical CP and appends one StoryChar to an unbounded Vec. The public read function and native convert command invoke this before any DOCX admission.
originalFinding.impact: For example, 1024 consecutive pieces can each reference the same 1 MiB physical text region while declaring a 1 GiB logical story. An approximately 1.1 MiB compound file then requests at least 12 GiB of StoryChar payload, before subsequent representations, causing memory exhaustion and process termination.
supporting_source_evidence: pieces reads each raw PCD offset independently and assigns fc: if compressed { fc / 2 } else { fc }.
main_text checks CP ordering and coverage, then loops for cp in piece.cp_start..end and calls out.push(StoryChar { ch, ..here }).
read calls main_text using the attacker-controlled FIB ccp_text.
The CLI calls legacy_doc::doc_to_docx before its admit_word branch, which explicitly excludes legacy input.
counterevidence: Individual physical character accesses use checked offsets and get, preventing an out-of-bounds read.
Compound-file chain lengths and FAT duplication have explicit controls; those controls do not bound logical CP expansion.
The CP field is u32, but its possible decoded allocation remains far larger than typical process memory.
No application code was executed.
originalFinding.remediation: Introduce a configurable legacy-input resource budget and reject excessive ccp_text, total decoded records, and cumulative piece expansion before allocating or iterating. Charge reused physical ranges against the decoded-output budget.

candidate.originalEvidence: Story::blocks at legacy_doc.rs:1605 computes fields.iter().any for every character, field begin pushes true, separator sets last false. Input repeating '\x13\x14' N times creates N false field levels; every subsequent pair scans all prior false levels. O(N²) on ~2N text bytes, no nesting/depth limit. read() and CLI convert reach it directly; separate from XML parser.

originalFinding.title: Nested legacy DOC field results cause quadratic processing
originalFinding.attacker: An attacker supplying a legacy DOC to the library or native CLI.
originalFinding.violated_security_invariant: Field interpretation must require bounded work per input character.
originalFinding.source_to_sink: Story::blocks retains one boolean per nested field and recomputes whether any ancestor contains field code by scanning the entire vector for every character. Repeating a field-begin byte followed by its separator creates arbitrarily many false ancestor entries. Every subsequent begin and separator scans all preceding false entries.
originalFinding.impact: A compact story composed of repeated byte pairs 0x13,0x14 produces quadratic CPU work. Appending matching 0x15 bytes gives balanced fields without removing the quadratic cost. A malicious document can occupy the conversion worker for a prolonged period.
supporting_source_evidence: For every story character, the implementation executes fields.iter().any(|&code| code).
0x13 pushes true; 0x14 sets the newest entry false; no nesting limit is applied.
A sequence of N begin/separator pairs therefore scans progressively longer false prefixes, totaling O(N squared) work.
counterevidence: The vector prevents recursive stack growth in this particular field parser.
The input sequence can be balanced and need not rely on malformed compound-file metadata.
ZIP XML-depth admission does not apply to legacy field nesting.
No timing experiment or application execution was performed.
originalFinding.remediation: Maintain an aggregate count of ancestors currently inside field code, updating it on push, separator, and pop, so in_code is constant time. Apply a maximum field nesting budget as additional protection.

candidate.originalEvidence: altchunk HTML <td colspan='1000000000'> parses usize at src/convert/altchunk.rs:563-567 and end_table emits one <w:gridCol> per span at 469-490, before any revalidation, so tiny admitted .html part triggers tens of GB output.

originalFinding.title: HTML altChunk colspan expands tiny input into arbitrarily large generated XML
originalFinding.attacker: An attacker supplying a DOCX containing an internal HTML or MHT altChunk to a public rendering or render-report API.
originalFinding.violated_invariant: Conversion from admitted package content to generated XML must retain resource limits across the representation change.
dataflow: src/convert/mod.rs:773-798 admits the original package, then expands w:altChunk before DOM construction.
mod.rs:791-792 resolves the relationship and reads bytes from the in-memory package.
src/convert/altchunk.rs:34-39 decodes the chunk and invokes html_to_wml.
altchunk.rs:562-566 parses td/th colspan as usize with no maximum.
altchunk.rs:469-475 calculates cols from the attacker-controlled span, then 489-490 emits one gridCol element per numeric column.
originalFinding.impact: An HTML chunk containing one td with colspan="1000000000" causes approximately tens of gigabytes of generated grid XML from a small package, exhausting memory or CPU before rendering. A larger accepted integer can keep emission running until process termination. This operation is independent of the raw DOCX table-grid allocation: it exhausts resources while constructing XML, before table_block is reached.
source_evidence: altchunk.rs:563-566 applies only parse::<usize>(), unwrap_or(1), and max(1) to colspan.
altchunk.rs:472 sums cell spans without a resource cap.
altchunk.rs:489-490 loops over 0..cols and appends to an unbounded String.
mod.rs:790-798 expands the chunk after original package admission and immediately parses the result without a generated-output budget.
altchunk.rs:1047-1055 tests zero/invalid/negative colspan fallback, but no upper bound is implemented.
counterevidence: Original archive and inflated HTML byte sizes are bounded by admission.
The chunk loader reads package bytes and does not fetch an external URL or host file.
Small ordinary colspan values are intentionally supported; the problem is attacker-selected numeric amplification rather than normal table conversion.
The bounded raster page allocator is downstream and cannot constrain XML generation.
This is a static source finding; no oversized input was executed.
originalFinding.remediation: Bound individual colspan and aggregate columns, use checked sums, and enforce an output-byte budget while generating WML. Return a conversion refusal when these budgets are exceeded. Apply equivalent bounds to HTML and MHT chunks before expensive construction.

candidate.originalEvidence: Raw admitted DOCX <w:gridSpan w:val='1000000000'/> parses without cap src/convert/mod.rs:14211-14216, occupancy drives vec![each; occupancy]/resize at 13604-13616. Both reachable render -> with_layout admission; budgets count bytes/depth but not numeric table width.

originalFinding.title: DOCX table span integers directly control unbounded renderer allocations
originalFinding.attacker: An attacker supplying a DOCX to public render, docx_to_png, PDF conversion, or render-report APIs.
originalFinding.violated_invariant: Admitted tiny XML must not directly select an arbitrarily large table-grid allocation.
dataflow: src/convert/mod.rs:592-615 exposes render and invokes with_layout.
with_layout at mod.rs:773-798 admits the package, loads document XML, and constructs its DOM.
table_block at mod.rs:13466-13535 obtains cell_span and stores the result in RawCell.colspan.
cell_span at mod.rs:14211-14215 parses w:gridSpan/@w:val as usize and applies only max(1).
table_block at mod.rs:13603-13615 sums these values into occupancy and uses occupancy directly in vec![each; occupancy] or Vec::resize.
originalFinding.impact: A shallow document containing one cell with w:gridSpan w:val="1000000000" requests a grid of one billion f32 values, followed by additional grid-sized structures. Larger values can cause allocation failure/capacity overflow and terminate the host. The value requires only a few input bytes and remains within archive, part-size, attribute-size, and XML-depth admission limits.
source_evidence: mod.rs:14211-14215 has no maximum on parsed gridSpan.
mod.rs:13604 sets occupancy from the sum of RawCell.colspan.
mod.rs:13609 allocates vec![each; occupancy]; mod.rs:13611 independently resizes to occupancy.
The sibling row_grid_skip path at mod.rs:14340-14345 likewise accepts any positive usize from gridBefore/gridAfter.
grid_skip_cell at mod.rs:14357-14379 assigns that span to RawCell.colspan, reaching the same allocation.
mod.rs:14262-14288 and 14603-14645 contain further span-sized iteration/allocation after the initial grid growth.
counterevidence: with_layout does perform package admission at mod.rs:773-774, using the compare budget through document_comparer.rs:4926-4927.
InputLimits bounds serialized bytes and XML nesting, not table span numeric magnitude.
stretch_stale_spans at mod.rs:14172-14177 leaves a span unchanged when its existing occupancy already exceeds the grid.
Raster page dimensions and DPI are bounded later, but the table allocation occurs during layout, including report-only requests.
No application execution or allocation experiment was performed.
originalFinding.remediation: Validate gridSpan, gridBefore, gridAfter, and aggregate row occupancy against a configurable table-column budget before constructing RawCell values or expanding vectors. Use checked addition and fallible allocation, and apply the same budget to subsequent span-sized loops and merge bookkeeping.

candidate.originalEvidence: HTML nested <table><tr><td> is accepted iteratively without depth cap, emits nested WML end_table; with_layout then calls infallible recursive Dom::parse_xdocument at 798 (Parser::parse_element recurses at xmllinq/parse.rs:661), bypassing admitted max_xml_depth. .html chunk is not checked by XML admission.

originalFinding.title: Nested HTML altChunks bypass XML-depth admission before a recursive DOM parse
originalFinding.attacker: An attacker supplying a DOCX with a deeply nested internal HTML altChunk.
originalFinding.violated_invariant: The XML-depth limit must apply to XML created from untrusted alternative representations before recursive DOM construction.
dataflow: with_layout at mod.rs:773-774 admits original package XML under InputLimits.
Admission identifies XML by .xml/.rels extension at src/admission.rs:535-545; an HTML chunk is treated as bounded binary content rather than subjected to XML nesting validation.
altchunk.rs:543-550 pushes a Table per HTML table, and 558-567 opens cell sinks without a nesting limit.
altchunk.rs:463-517 builds nested w:tbl/w:tr/w:tc content from the nested HTML tables.
mod.rs:798 invokes infallible Dom::parse_xdocument on the expanded XML.
src/xmllinq/parse.rs:555-661 recursively calls parse_element for each nested child without an internal depth guard.
originalFinding.impact: A shallow, admitted DOCX can carry many nested table/tr/td HTML levels in a small .html part. Conversion produces XML deeper than max_xml_depth, then the recursive parser can exhaust the thread stack and terminate the embedding process. This route requires no oversized colspan and remains after fixing numeric table-span amplification.
source_evidence: mod.rs:790-798 changes the admitted XML through altchunk::expand and passes the resulting string directly to parse_xdocument.
altchunk.rs:543-550 does not limit tables.len().
altchunk.rs:498-508 embeds cell.wml, retaining nested table content when it contains a paragraph.
xmllinq/parse.rs:90-98 explicitly documents that parse_xdocument does not enforce policy.
xmllinq/parse.rs:660-662 recursively parses every child element.
The checked alternative at xmllinq/parse.rs:129-135 validates depth before DOM construction but is not used here.
counterevidence: Original .xml/.rels parts are admitted with max_xml_depth=256.
The HTML reader itself uses iterative stacks, so it does not necessarily fail before the deeper XML reaches the recursive parser.
Exact crash depth depends on platform and stack size; no triggering input was executed.
Process-level quotas remain useful, but they do not restore the skipped XML-depth check or prevent a host stack abort.
originalFinding.remediation: Enforce HTML table nesting and generated-WML byte budgets during expansion. Validate the expanded XML with the active InputLimits, or use try_parse_xdocument_with_limits, before recursive DOM construction.

No exclusive creation/random/private dir. Native secure UUID staging is not called.
candidate.pythonSibling: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:407-411 target=os.path.realpath(plan), partial=target.with_name(f'.{target.name}.{os.getpid()}.partial'), partial.write_bytes(...), os.replace(partial,target). originalFinding.title: Predictable plan staging filenames permit symlink-based arbitrary file truncation
originalFinding.attacker: A local attacker able to create files in a directory where another user records an edit plan.
originalFinding.violated_security_invariant: Recording a plan must only modify its authorized destination and securely created staging storage.
originalFinding.source_to_sink: Both hosted CLIs derive their temporary filename solely from the target basename and process PID, then write to it using ordinary truncating file writes. An attacker can precreate that predictable .partial pathname as a symlink to a file writable by the victim. The staging write follows the link and overwrites the referent before the subsequent rename.
originalFinding.impact: When the victim records operations with edit/add --plan in a shared writable directory, the attacker can clobber a different victim-writable file with the generated plan JSON. This can corrupt configuration or other sensitive files outside the requested plan destination.
supporting_source_evidence: Python constructs partial = target.with_name(f".{target.name}.{os.getpid()}.partial") and calls partial.write_bytes before os.replace.
Node constructs `.${path.basename(target)}.${process.pid}.partial` and calls fs.writeFileSync before fs.renameSync.
Neither path uses exclusive creation, a no-follow open, unpredictable secure temporary storage, or the native publication staging API.
counterevidence: The attacker needs local directory-write access and knowledge or prediction of the victim process PID.
Plan preview must succeed before the vulnerable write.
Resolving the final plan target does not secure the subsequently constructed temporary pathname.
